  comment = "#>",
  eval = identical(Sys.getenv("RCEATTLE_EVAL_VIGNETTES"), "true")

This is the menu of options you choose between when configuring a `data_list`
and the arguments to `fit_mod()`. Vignette 1,
[Rceattle: An Introduction](introduction.html), fits a model end to end;
vignette 8, [Model parameterizations](model-parameterizations.html), is the
equation-level reference (in progress); and vignettes 2-7 cover HCRs and MSEs,
diagnostics, projections and reference points, single- vs. multi-species models,
building a data object in R, and Stock Synthesis migration.

## 1. Model dimensions and operating mode

> Equations: see vignette 8 [§Population dynamics](model-parameterizations.html#population-dynamics).

| Switch | Where set | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `nspp`, `nages`, `nsex`, `nlengths` | `data_list` | Population structure |
| `styr`, `endyr`, `projyr` | `data_list` | Time horizon (hindcast + projection) |
| `msmMode` | `fit_mod()` | Single- vs. multi-species |
| `initMode` | `fit_mod()` | Initial age structure |
| `estimateMode` | `fit_mod()` | Estimate / project / debug |
| `random_rec`, `random_q`, `random_sel` | `fit_mod()` | Random-effects toggles |

### `msmMode`, single-species vs. multi-species

| Value | Meaning | Status |
|:---:|---|---|
| `0` | Single-species (M = M1 only) | Validated |
| `1` | Multi-species, MSVPA Type II predation | Validated |
| `2` | Multi-species, MSVPA Type III predation | Validated |
| `3:9` | Kinzey & Punt (2009) functional responses (Holling I/II/III, predator interference, predator preemption, Hassell-Varley, Ecosim) | **Not implemented**: `fit_mod()` rejects them as invalid `msmMode` codes |

### `initMode`, initial age structure

Codes (also accept the string aliases listed):

| Value | Alias | Description |
|:---:|---|---|
| `0` | `"FreeParams"` | Initial N-at-age estimated as free parameters, started at the unfished equilibrium of R0 and female M1 (at log numbers 0, i.e. 1 thousand fish per age, under a single-species stock-recruit curve) |
| `1` | `"Equilibrium"` | Unfished equilibrium, no init devs, F<sub>init</sub> = 0 |
| `2` (default) | `"NonEquilibrium"` | Unfished equilibrium with initial deviations |
| `3` | `"FishedNonEquilibrium"` | Fished non-equilibrium with init devs; F<sub>init</sub> is added to M inside geometric series |
| `4` | `"FishedNonEquilibriumScaled"` | Fished non-equilibrium with init devs and R<sub>0</sub>-scaled by F<sub>init</sub>|
| `5` | `"OffsetEquilibrium"` | Unfished equilibrium, F<sub>init</sub> = 0, displaced by the year-1 recruitment deviation instead of sitting at R<sub>init</sub>; init devs off, no init-dev penalty (Cole Monnahan / AFSC GOA pollock convention) |
| `6` | `"FishedNonEquilibriumSelected"` | As `3`, but F<sub>init</sub> is weighted by the fishery's selectivity at age before it accumulates, so the first year decays with &sum;(M1 + F<sub>init</sub> s<sub>a</sub>). Stock Synthesis's InitF convention; F<sub>init</sub> is the apical initial F. Use this where the fishery is size-selective, since `3` charges unselected young ages the full F<sub>init</sub> and `4` applies it once |

F<sub>init</sub> is one per species (SS3 carries one per fleet), so under mode
`6` a species with more than one fishery decays its initial age structure at the
**mean** selectivity of those fisheries, F<sub>init</sub> is the apical initial F
of none of them, and `data_check()` warns.

#### The initial equilibrium catch

Modes `3`, `4` and `6` estimate F<sub>init</sub>, but nothing identifies it
without an observation: the catch taken under it in the year before the
hindcast. Enter it as an ordinary `catch_data` row at `styr - 1`, with the
fleet's `Catch` and `Log_sd`. **It is read only under mode `6`**, the one mode
that builds the initial age structure with the mortality the prediction uses
(Baranov at F<sub>init</sub> &times; selectivity); under any other mode the row
is dropped, and `data_check()` says so.

That year also holds ordinary catch history, so `data_check()` names the fleets
whose rows it reads. It refuses two rows for one fleet, a non-positive catch or
`Log_sd`, a fleet that is not an active fishery, and a species with more than one
fishery. `clean_data()` moves the row into `data_list$equil_catch_data`, and
`write_data()` writes it back into the catch sheet. The prediction is
`quantities$equil_catch_hat`, scored on the `jnll_comp` row
`"Initial equilibrium catch"`.

### `estimateMode`, what does `fit_mod()` actually do?

| Value | Behavior |
|:---:|---|
| `0` | Estimate hindcast and projection parameters via `nlminb` / `TMB::sdreport` (default). |
| `1` | Estimate only the hindcast parameters via `nlminb` / `TMB::sdreport`. |
| `2` | Hold the hindcast fixed and run only the projection under the supplied `HCR`. |
| `3` | Evaluate the report once at `inits` (debug / mapping check). |
| `4` | Run through `MakeADFun` and `nlminb` with all parameters mapped out (debug / mapping check). |

### Random-effects toggles

`random_rec`, `random_q` and `random_sel` move the log-recruitment,
log-catchability and time-varying selectivity deviations from penalized fixed
effects to random effects, marginalized by the Laplace approximation with their
distribution parameters estimated.

## 2. Predation: `suitMode` (per predator)

> Equations: see vignette 8 [§Predation sub-model](model-parameterizations.html#predation-sub-model) (suitability, predation mortality, consumption / bioenergetics).

`suitMode` sets how prey preference is modelled; length 1 (all predators) or `nspp`.

| Value | String | Description | Available? |
|:---:|---|---|:---:|
| `0` | `"Empirical"` | Empirical proportions from observed stomach data (MSVPA-style; Holsman et al. 2016) | Yes |
| `1` | `"GammaLength"` | Gamma suitability on prey length-at-age | **Not yet** |
| `2` | `"GammaWeight"` | Gamma suitability on prey weight-at-age | Yes |
| `3` | `"LognormalLength"` | Log-normal suitability on prey length-at-age | **Not yet** |
| `4` | `"LognormalWeight"` | Log-normal suitability on prey weight-at-age | Yes |
| `5` | `"NormalLength"` | Normal suitability on prey length-at-age | **Not yet** |
| `6` | `"NormalWeight"` | Normal suitability on prey weight-at-age | Yes |

Where year-specific diet data are not supplied (`Year = 0` in `diet_data`),
suitability is averaged across `suit_styr:suit_endyr`, the full hindcast by
default.

A *predicted* diet needs estimated suitability **and** a predation model:
`suitMode` 2, 4 or 6 with `msmMode > 0`. Under `suitMode = 0` suitability is read
from `diet_data`, and under `msmMode = 0` no predation is computed, so neither
has a fitted diet; `residuals(source = "diet")`, `plot_diet_comp()`,
`plot_diet_comp1()` and `plot_diet_comp2()` refuse on such a fit.

## 3. Selectivity (per fleet)

> Equations: see vignette 8 [§Selectivity parameterizations](model-parameterizations.html#selectivity-parameterizations).

Set the `Selectivity` column of `fleet_control`; integers and strings both work:

| Value | String | Notes |
|:---:|---|---|
| `0` | `"Fixed"` | Selectivity supplied via the `emp_sel` data sheet |
| `1` | `"Logistic"` | Two-parameter ascending logistic |
| `2` | `"NonParametric"` | Age- or length-bin-indexed; penalties via `Sel_curve_pen1` / `Sel_curve_pen2` |
| `3` | `"DoubleLogistic"` | Dome-shaped (ascending + descending logistic) |
| `4` | `"DescendingLogistic"` | Descending only |
| `5` | `"Hake"` | Non-parametric à la Taylor et al. (Pacific hake) |
| `6` | `"2DAR1"` | 2D AR(1) bin × year (Xu et al. 2019) |
| `7` | `"3DAR1"` | 3D AR(1) bin × year × cohort (Cheng et al. 2023) |
| `8` | `"DoubleNormal"` | Four-parameter double normal: peak, ascending and descending widths, and a right-tail floor (the Stock Synthesis pattern 24 shape without its initial-selectivity and plateau-width parameters) |
| `9` | `"NonParametricPM"` | Ianelli non-parametric with the ADMB AMAK ("pm") penalty; see `Sel_avgsel_pen`, `Sel_cap_bin` |
| `11` | `"LogisticPM"` | AMAK ("pm") logistic: multiplicative inflection/slope deviations plus a free age-1 log-selectivity |
| `13` | `"NonParametricIntegrable"` | The `NonParametric` base curve whose deviations have a proper density: the shape penalties are charged once on the base, so `random_sel = TRUE` integrates them |
| `15` | `"DoubleNormalSS3"` | Stock Synthesis size pattern 24: the six-parameter double normal, each parameter on SS3's own scale (peak; logit top width; log ascending and descending widths; logit initial and final selectivity) in its own array `sel_dn6`. An end left at SS3's -999 is unscaled and fixed. Not normalized, as in SS3. All six take selectivity linkages under the SS3 manual's names; `Time_varying_sel` must be `"Off"` |

Codes `10`, `12` and `14` are unused.

The AR(1) forms reuse the `Sel_curve_pen` columns as logit-scale correlations,
one per dimension: `Sel_curve_pen1` across selectivity **bins** (ages or length
bins, per `Selectivity_dimension`), `Sel_curve_pen2` across **years**, and
`Sel_curve_pen3` across **cohorts** for `3DAR1`.

Time-varying behavior is set by `Time_varying_sel` (per fleet):

| Value | String | Behavior |
|:---:|---|---|
| `0` | `"Off"` | Time-invariant |
| `1` | `"IID"` | Independent annual deviations |
| `2` | `"AR1"` | **Removed in 5.16.0**: `data_check()` errors on it. Set `"IID"` for the same fit, or see the replacement below. |
| `3` | `"Block"` | Time block |
| `4` | `"RandomWalk"` | Random walk |
| `5` | `"RandomWalkAscending"` | Random walk on ascending portion of double logistic |

Not every mode applies to every selectivity form:

| Selectivity | Modes accepted |
|---|---|
| `Logistic`, `DoubleLogistic`, `DescendingLogistic`, `DoubleNormal` | `Off`, `IID`, `Block`, `RandomWalk`; `RandomWalkAscending` on `DoubleLogistic` only. On another form, link its ascending parameters instead (`peak` / `sigma_asc` for `DoubleNormal`, `inf_asc` / `slp_asc` for the logistic family) with `~ rw(1 \| Year)` |
| `NonParametric` | `Off`, `IID`, `RandomWalk` |
| `NonParametricPM` | `Off`, `RandomWalk`: its deviates *are* the walk increments, so `IID` would describe a different curve than the model builds |
| `NonParametricIntegrable` | `Off`, `IID`, `RandomWalk`; `Off` estimates no deviations |
| `Hake` | `Off`, `IID` |
| `2DAR1`, `3DAR1` | none; the field's correlations come from `Sel_curve_pen`, and its conditional sd from `Time_varying_sel_sd`, which they always need |

The two non-parametric modes differ in what they are a deviation *of*, and
**`fit_mod()` refuses `random_sel = TRUE` on both**:

* **`"IID"`** scores each annual coefficient deviation about an estimated base
  curve. The density is proper, but the AMAK shape penalties (`Sel_curve_pen1`,
  `Sel_curve_pen2`) and the always-on average-selectivity term are charged on
  each year's realized curve, and none scales with `Time_varying_sel_sd`, so the
  estimated sd is biased low whatever the penalty weights.
* **`"RandomWalk"`** scores the year-to-year change in the *realized*
  selectivity, which is renormalized to mean 1 within each year. Its density says
  nothing about the level of a year's coefficients, so those directions are
  improper and the deviation standard deviation collapses to zero.

Fit them with `random_sel = FALSE`, the penalized formulation the AMAK model
intends, or use `NonParametricIntegrable` (code `13` above) with
`random_sel = TRUE`.

Even under `NonParametricIntegrable`, the Laplace approximation underestimates
the deviation SD on small multinomial samples (a true 0.35 came back at 0.24 to
0.26 on `Atka2022`'s fishery), so read it as a lower bound unless the
compositions are well sampled.

`Time_varying_sel` is **soft-deprecated as a whole**, and `data_check()` says so
on use. The linkage grammar expresses the same IID, random-walk and AR(1)
deviations (`(1 | Year)`, `rw(1 | Year)`, `ar1(1 | Year)`) and
[time blocks](environmental-linkages-and-priors.html#time-blocks)
(`~ cut(Year, ...)`) per selectivity *parameter* rather than per fleet, and lets
the deviation standard deviation be estimated, given a prior, or held fixed:

```r
build_selectivity(linkages = list(
  inf_asc = linkage_spec(~ ar1(1 | Year), by = ~ fleet)))
```

Name whichever parameter should vary: `slp_asc`, `inf_asc`, `slp_desc`,
`inf_desc`, or a `DoubleNormal` alias. `apical`, the height of one sex's curve
relative to the other's, is available on every estimated form except `2DAR1` and
`3DAR1`, on a two-sex species; see
[Environmental linkages and priors](environmental-linkages-and-priors.html#selectivity).

Bin indexing: with non-parametric and AR(1) forms, selectivity is
indexed over `N_sel_bins`.

`Sel_norm_bin` says where selectivity is normalized to 1. Set it to `"Max"` to
normalize by the largest value (non-differentiable), to `"Off"` to leave the
curve unnormalized, or to a bin to normalize there. Give `Sel_norm_bin_upper` as
well and the reference is mean selectivity over that range instead.

A numeric `Sel_norm_bin` is read on the fleet's own `Selectivity_dimension`: an
absolute **age** for an age-based fleet (`6` means age 6, not the sixth bin) or
a 1-based **length-bin ordinal** for a length-based one. `Bin_first_selected`
beside it uses the opposite convention and is always a bin ordinal. Below
`Bin_first_selected` the curve is zeroed, so a reference taken there would divide
by nothing; such a value is read as `"Max"`, which is what a negative has always
meant. Legacy numbers still work: blank is `"Off"`, and `0`, `-1` or `-999` are
`"Max"`.

### Sharing a selectivity between fleets

Fleets given the same `Selectivity_index` share one selectivity parameter block,
and its penalties and priors are accumulated once, on the group's first non-`Off`
fleet. The columns that shape the curve are still read **per fleet**, so they
have to agree across the group or the fleets end up with different selectivities:

| Column | If it differs within the group |
|---|---|
| `Selectivity`, `Selectivity_dimension`, `Bin_first_selected`, `N_sel_bins`, `Sel_norm_bin`, `Sel_norm_bin_upper`, `Sel_norm_scope`, `Sel_cap_bin` | The fleets get **different curves**: mirroring fails |
| `Time_varying_sel` | Resolved to the lead fleet's setting |
| `Sel_start_year` | Resolved to the group's earliest year |
| `Time_varying_sel_sd` | Honoured per fleet while it is **fixed**. Under `random_sel = TRUE` the group estimates one deviation sd, starting at the *geometric* mean of its estimated members' values, so no fleet keeps its own. `build_map()` warns |

A blank counts as a value in the first row: an unset `Sel_norm_bin` (written back
as `"Off"`) means "do not normalize", which is a different curve from normalizing
at a bin. `data_check()` warns in all three cases, distinguishing divergence from
resolution.

The reliable way to mirror a fleet is to copy its `fleet_control` row and change
only the identity and catchability columns:

```r
mirror <- fleet_control[fleet_control$Fleet_name == "Fishery", ]
mirror$Fleet_name         <- "Fishery_CPUE"
mirror$Fleet_code         <- nrow(fleet_control) + 1L
mirror$Fleet_type         <- "Survey"
mirror$Catchability_index <- mirror$Fleet_code
fleet_control <- rbind(fleet_control, mirror)
```

### Sex structure and relative selectivity

**Every selectivity form is sex-specific by default** when a species has two
sexes (`nsex`): each sex gets its own free copy of every selectivity parameter.

Two independent normalization columns decide whether the sexes keep a
*relative* scale or differ only in shape:

* **`Sel_norm_bin`, where the reference is taken**, as above.
* **`Sel_norm_scope`, whose scale it sets.** `"AcrossSexes"` (default) pools one
  reference over the sexes, so the less-selected sex stays below 1 and
  **relative sex-specific selectivity is retained**. `"WithinSex"` divides each
  sex by its own reference, so both reach 1 and only the *shape* differs by sex.

| `Sel_norm_bin` | `Sel_norm_scope` | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `"Off"` | (any) | nothing normalized; the relative scale is free |
| `"Max"` | `"AcrossSexes"` | maximum over bins **and sexes**: one sex peaks at 1, the other keeps whatever relative level its form gives it |
| `"Max"` | `"WithinSex"` | each sex scaled at **its own plateau**, wherever that falls |
| a bin | `"AcrossSexes"` | anchored at that bin, sexes kept comparable |
| a bin | `"WithinSex"` | both sexes forced to 1 at that bin; only the shape differs |

For strongly dimorphic stocks the relative sex selectivity is usually the
quantity of interest, so keep the `"AcrossSexes"` default. Where the sexes
plateau at different ages and each should be scaled at its own plateau, use
`Sel_norm_bin = "Max"` with `Sel_norm_scope = "WithinSex"` rather than a named
bin, which stops being the plateau once selectivity is time-varying.

`Sel_norm_scope` has no effect on a one-sex species, or where `Sel_norm_bin` is
`"Off"`.

#### Which forms can hold a sex difference in level

`"AcrossSexes"` normalization *preserves* a level ratio and cannot create one,
so whether the sexes can reach different levels at all is a property of the
**form**. (`"WithinSex"` at a named bin divides each sex by its own value
there, so two sexes whose curves differ in shape end on different plateaus.)

| Form | Sex difference in level, from the form alone |
|---|---|
| `Logistic`, `DescendingLogistic`, `LogisticPM` | **none**: the curve tends to 1 for either sex, whatever its parameters |
| `NonParametric`, `NonParametricPM`, `NonParametricIntegrable` | **none**: each sex is re-centred so its own mean selectivity-at-age is exactly 1, every year |
| `Hake` | **none**: normalizes within sex by its own maximum; `Sel_norm_scope` is not read (nor by `LogisticPM`, which is not normalized at all) |
| `DoubleNormal` | **old-age plateau only**: the right-tail floor is sex-specific, but both sexes peak at exactly 1 |
| `DoubleLogistic`, `2DAR1`, `3DAR1` | **free**: the height is a free function of that sex's own parameters |

Every row above describes the form on its own. An `apical` selectivity linkage
adds a per-sex height multiplier to any estimated form but `2DAR1`/`3DAR1`,
applied after the form's own centring and before `Sel_norm_bin` normalization
(so `Sel_norm_scope` must be `"AcrossSexes"`, or `Sel_norm_bin` `"Off"`), so a "none" here means the
shape cannot hold the difference, not that the model cannot. `data_check()` notes the unread
`Sel_norm_scope` on a two-sex `Hake` or `LogisticPM` fleet left on the default
`"AcrossSexes"`; `LogisticPM` reuses `Sel_norm_bin` as a penalty bin range.

On a two-sex `Logistic` fleet an `apical` linkage gives five parameters: slope
and inflection per sex, plus one height multiplier on the sex named. Only the
joint-sex rows (`Sex = 3`) inform that height. Unlike a Stock Synthesis male
offset, usually an offset from the female *shape*, both shapes stay free; sharing
a shape across the sexes needs a hand-edited `map` that points one sex's cells
at the other's.

**The composition data must be joint.** `comp_data$Sex = 3` stacks female and
male composition into a single vector that is normalized to sum to 1 as a whole
(as Stock Synthesis does), so the sex ratio is fit and the relative selectivity
is informed. `Sex = 1` or `2` put each sex in its own row, each summing to 1
independently: those hold **no** sex-ratio information, and `Sel_norm_bin` then
makes no difference however it is set. There is no separate sex-ratio likelihood
component.

The sex ratio at recruitment is **fixed input**, not estimated, from the
`sex_ratio` sheet at the first modelled age. Sex-specific natural mortality is
`build_M1(M1_model = )` (§7) and sex-specific growth is `build_growth()` (§8);
the linkage grammar's per-sex hooks are `linkage_spec(by = ~ sex)` and its
`sex =` filter. The `fleet_control` `Sex` column is **inert**, kept only so older
workbooks still read; sex is set per observation on `comp_data`.

## 4. Catchability (per fleet)

> Equations: see vignette 8 [§Catchability parameterizations](model-parameterizations.html#catchability-parameterizations).

Set the `Catchability` column of `fleet_control`:

| Value | String | Description |
|:---:|---|---|
| `0` | `"Fixed"` | q supplied directly |
| `1` | `"Estimated"` | q estimated as a free parameter |
| `2` | `"Estimated-with-prior"` | Estimated with a lognormal prior on q: mean `Catchability_init` (median when `bias_adjust_proc = FALSE`), log-scale SD `Catchability_prior_sd` |
| `3` | `"Analytical"` | The closed-form maximum likelihood q for the fleet's `Index_distribution` (concentrated likelihood). Refused under `TruncatedNormal`, which has no closed-form q |
| `4` | `"PowerEquation"` | Power-function catchability (q · B<sup>α</sup>). **Not implemented**: `data_check()` rejects it. |
| `5` | `"Environmental"` | q linked to an environmental index. **Deprecated in 4.9.0**: express it as a covariate linkage instead, `build_catchability(linkages = list(q = linkage_spec(~ temp, by = ~ fleet)))`. The series is named by `Time_varying_q`, not `Catchability_index`. |
| `6` | `"AR1"` | **Removed in 5.12.0**: `data_check()` errors on it. Its deviates were never estimated, so q came back constant. Express the Rogers et al. (2024) form as a q linkage instead, see below. |
| `7` | `"AnalyticalArith"` | q solved from the fleet's own index observations using the AMAK arithmetic-mean estimator; pair with `Index_distribution = "MVN"` for a supplied covariance |

### Index likelihood (`Index_distribution`)

How an index observation is scored, per fleet. The choice also sets how
residuals and plot intervals are computed.

| Value | String | Scale | Description |
|:---:|---|---|---|
| `0` | `"Lognormal"` | log | Independent lognormal on `log(obs)`. The default. `Log_sd` is a log-scale CV. |
| `1` | `"MVN"` | natural | The AMAK/`ebswp` `DoCovBTS = 1` bare quadratic form `0.5 · r' Σ⁻¹ r` on the residual `obs − q·pred`. Drops the normalizing constant, so the reported value matches ADMB. Needs `index_cov`. |
| `2` | `"MVNORM"` | natural | The full multivariate-normal negative log-density. Identical fit to `"MVN"` (the extra term is constant), but properly normalized. Needs `index_cov`. |
| `3` | `"Normal"` | natural | Normal on `obs − q·pred`, with `Log_sd` read as an **absolute** natural-scale sd, not a CV. No lognormal bias correction. |
| `4` | `"TruncatedNormal"` | natural | The same normal, left-truncated at zero. An index cannot be negative, so this is the only natural-scale family whose simulator and likelihood are the same distribution. **Prefer it over `"Normal"`** unless you need an exact ADMB comparison. `data_check()` refuses it with `Catchability = "Analytical"`. |

Time-varying behavior is set by `Time_varying_q` (per fleet):

| Value | String | Behavior |
|:---:|---|---|
| `0` | `"Off"` | Time-invariant |
| `1` | `"IID"` | Independent annual deviations |
| `2` | `"AR1"` | **Removed in 5.16.0**: `data_check()` errors on it. Set `"IID"` for the same fit, or see the replacement below. |
| `3` | `"Block"` | Time block |
| `4` | `"RandomWalk"` | Random walk |

`Time_varying_q` is **soft-deprecated as a whole**, as `Time_varying_sel` is,
and `data_check()` says so on use; the linkage grammar expresses the same
deviations and [time blocks](environmental-linkages-and-priors.html#time-blocks),
with the deviation standard deviation estimated, given a prior, or held fixed:

```r
build_catchability(linkages = list(
  q = linkage_spec(~ ar1(1 | Year), by = ~ fleet)))
```

The removed `Catchability = "AR1"` (QAR1, Rogers et al. 2024) is the same
formula plus the series the deviations are *observed* against, which makes it
the state-space form rather than a free AR(1) on q:

```r
build_catchability(linkages = list(
  q = linkage_spec(~ ar1(1 | Year), by = ~ fleet, fleet = <Fleet_code>,
                   observe = "<that fleet's env_data column>",
                   obs_sd  = <its measurement SD>)))
```

Under `Catchability = "Environmental"`, `Time_varying_q` instead names the
`env_data` series to use: an integer, or a string of them (`"1,2,3"`).

### Which fleets get a catchability

Catchability follows the **data**, not the fleet type. A fleet is given a q if it
holds `index_data` the model fits, a fishery with a CPUE series as much as a
survey. A fishery's index is predicted from that fishery's own selectivity; an
index needing a *different* selectivity has to be its own fleet, since
`sel_at_age` is one block per fleet (the same is true of `Observation_units`).

A fleet with no fitted index rows gets **no** q, whatever `Catchability` says,
since nothing would inform it; that includes a composition-only survey. `print()`
marks the case:

```
[2] Fishery │ Fishery │ sel: Logistic │ q: Estimated (fixed: no index data)
```

The exception is sharing. Fleets with the same `Catchability_index` share one q
parameter, so the **lead** fleet (the group's first non-`Off` fleet) decides for
all of them whether it is estimated, regardless of type: a fleet with no index of
its own is still estimated if its lead is, and an `"Estimated"` fleet is still
fixed if its lead is `"Fixed"`. Give a fleet its own `Catchability_index` when it
should be estimated independently. Within a group:

* **`"Analytical"` / `"AnalyticalArith"`** solve q from each fleet's own index
  observations, so a group containing one does **not** share a catchability, even
  when every fleet in it holds the same setting. Give those fleets their own
  `Catchability_index`, or use an estimated q for the whole group.
* **`"Environmental"`** *does* share: the whole group follows the lead fleet,
  including its environmental series where the fleets name different ones in
  `Time_varying_q`.
* **A `"Fixed"` lead** estimates and shares nothing: each fleet sits at its own
  `Catchability_init`.
* **An estimated q** starts at the mean of the group's log `Catchability_init`,
  not the lead's; only the prior centre uses the lead's. `build_map()` warns when
  those inits differ and names the geometric mean: a shared q starting there
  scales a survey's whole predicted index by a constant factor, which no residual
  pattern distinguishes from a real change in abundance.
* **`Time_varying_q_sd`**, once estimated (`random_q = TRUE` with
  `Time_varying_q` of `"IID"` or `"RandomWalk"`), is one sd for the group,
  starting at the geometric mean of its estimated members' values, and
  `build_map()` warns when they differ. While fixed, each fleet keeps its own.
* **`Catchability_prior_sd`** is read only on the lead, where the prior is scored
  once.

`data_check()` warns on the analytical case, on a `Fixed` lead that leaves fleets
on different inits, and on a `Catchability` or `Time_varying_q` that differs
within a group.

### How an index is timed against mortality

The index prediction depends on `Fleet_type`; there is no column to set.

A **survey** index is a snapshot at the month given in `index_data`:

$$\hat{I}_y = q \sum_a s_a\, N_{a,y}\, e^{-(\text{Month}/12) Z_{a,y}}\, w_a$$

A **fishery** index is CPUE, which integrates over the year alongside the catch.
Baranov gives $C_a = F_a \bar{N}_a$, and effort cancels the $F$ (since
$F_a = q_e E s_a$):

$$\hat{I}_y = q \sum_a s_a\, \bar{N}_{a,y}\, w_a,
\qquad \bar{N}_{a,y} = N_{a,y}\frac{1 - e^{-Z_{a,y}}}{Z_{a,y}}$$

The catch equation and a fishery's age composition use the same $\bar{N}$, so a
fleet's index, catch, and comps are consistent. `Month` is not read for a
fishery's index rows.

This affects trend, not just scale, so a constant $q$ cannot absorb it. At
`Month = 6`, $e^{-Z/2}$ is 1.0% below $\bar{N}/N$ at $Z = 0.5$ but 8.8%
below at $Z = 1.5$; at `Month = 0` the snapshot factor is $e^0 = 1$, against
$\bar{N}/N$ of 0.906 at $Z = 0.2$ and 0.432 at $Z = 2.0$. A seasonal fishery
needs no special treatment: its exact window predictor differs from the
year-average by a near-constant factor $q$ takes up (1–3% trend error across
$F$ 0.05–0.8 for $M$ between 0.1 and 0.5, against 29–33% for a snapshot).

### A snapshot-timed index on a fishery's selectivity

This is the AMAK/ebswp CPUE form, and what an ADMB bridge needs. Give the index
its own `Survey` fleet and point that fleet's `Selectivity_index` at the fishery,
so the index gets the fishery's selectivity along with its own `Month` and its
own q. Build the mirror by copying the fishery's `fleet_control` row; see
[Sharing a selectivity between fleets](#sharing-a-selectivity-between-fleets)
for the columns that have to agree.

## 5. Composition likelihoods

Set `Comp_distribution` (or `CAAL_distribution`) per fleet:

| Value | String |
|:---:|---|
| `-1` | `"MultinomialAFSC"` (AFSC convention; the `Comp_distribution` default) |
| `0` | `"Multinomial"` (the `CAAL_distribution` default) |
| `1` | `"DirichletMultinomial"` (Thorson et al. 2017) |

Diet composition uses an analogous switch on the bioenergetics control sheet:
`Diet_distribution = 0` (multinomial) or `1` (Dirichlet-multinomial).
Conditional age-at-length (CAAL) data go through their own data path and are
weighted via `CAAL_weights` per fleet.

### Ageing error, per fleet

`age_error` holds one matrix per species by default, and every fleet reads its
own species'. A stock whose ageing protocol changed part way through a series
needs more than one (GOA Pacific cod reads its pre-2007 survey otoliths about a
year older than its post-2007 ones), so both `age_error` and `fleet_control`
take an optional `Ageing_error_index`: give the matrices index values, then point
each fleet at the one that aged its samples. Omit the column, or leave it `NA`,
and the index is the species. The two eras of a survey are then two fleets
sharing a `Selectivity_index` and a `Catchability_index`.

Each index belongs to one species, since a matrix's rows are sized by that
species' age range. `data_check()` refuses an index that names no matrix, an
index whose rows give more than one `Species`, and a fleet pointed at a matrix
belonging to another species (without the column, `2` means "species 2's
matrix", not "the second matrix"), and reports coverage per matrix.

## 6. Recruitment / stock-recruit (`recFun = build_srr()`)

| `srr_fun` | String | Description |
|:---:|---|---|
| `0` | `"mean"` | Mean recruitment with deviations |
| `2` | `"BevertonHolt"` | Beverton-Holt |
| `4` | `"Ricker"` | Ricker |

Priors and environmental relationships go on the curve through `build_srr()`;
see `?build_srr` and `vignette("environmental-linkages-and-priors")`.

Under multispecies mode (`msmMode > 0`) spawning biomass per recruit is
undefined, because mortality includes predation. A curve fitted in the
hindcast then estimates its initial recruitment level instead of deriving it,
and the choice of `initMode` can move the fitted stock substantially; the curve
can also enter as a recruitment penalty (`srr_fun = "mean"` with the curve as
`srr_pred_fun`). A prior on Beverton-Holt steepness is refused.

## 7. Natural mortality (`M1Fun = build_M1()`)

### `M1_model`, fixed-effects structure of M1

| Value | String | Description |
|:---:|---|---|
| `0` | `"fixed"` | use the input `M1_base` (no estimation). |
| `1` | `"sex_age_invariant"` | estimate one `M1_{spp}`. |
| `2` | `"sex_specific"` | estimate `M1_{spp, sex}`. |
| `3` | `"sex_age_specific"` | estimate `M1_{spp, sex, age}`. |

Priors and environmental relationships go on M1 through `build_M1()`; see
`?build_M1` and `vignette("environmental-linkages-and-priors")`.

### `M1_re`, random-effects structure on M1

| Value | String | Description |
|:---:|---|---|
| `0` (default) | `"none"`  | No random effects |
| `1` | `"iid_age"` | IID by age, constant over years |
| `2` | `"iid_year"` | IID by year, constant over ages |
| `3` |  `"iid_age_year"` | IID across both year and age |
| `4` | `"ar1_age"`  | AR(1) by age, constant over years |
| `5` | `"ar1_year"`| AR(1) by year, constant over ages |
| `6` | `"ar1_age_year"` | 2D AR(1) over both year and age |

`M1_re > 0` requires an `M1_model` of `0`, `1` or `2`, or `3` with a by-year
family (`2` or `5`). Under `M1_model = 0` the input schedule is held fixed and
the deviations carry all of M's variation, which makes them the most identifiable
of any level. Under `M1_model = 3` an age-varying deviation (`1`, `3`, `4`, `6`)
and the age-specific level enter the likelihood only as their sum;
`M1_model = 1` with `M1_re = 4` is the identifiable version of that model. The
deprecated env-driven `M1_model` `4` and `5` are refused for every family;
`linkage_spec(~ temp + (1 | Year))` expresses the same model.

Variance and correlation parameters are species-specific but
sex-invariant. `M1_dev_log_sd` is the AR(1) **innovation** standard deviation;
the marginal is `sigma / sqrt(1 - rho^2)`, as in WHAM. (The linkage grammar uses
the opposite convention: `linkage_spec(~ ar1(1 | Year), init = ...)` takes
`sigma` as the marginal SD.) `M2_use_prior = TRUE` adds a log-normal prior with
mean `M_prior` (the median when `bias_adjust_proc = FALSE`) and log-scale SD
`M_prior_sd` on total M (M1 + M2) in multi-species mode.

Modes `3` and `6` estimate a full age × year deviation field which, with a single
standard deviation and no prior on M, is strongly confounded with selectivity and
recruitment in a single-species assessment. Read `fit$convergence` and the
estimability table before trusting one, and consider a prior on M.

## 8. Growth and weight-at-age (`growthFun = build_growth()`)

### `fun` (`growth_model`): fixed-effects growth

| Value | String | Description |
|:---:|---|---|
| `0` (default) | `"empirical"` |  Empirical weight-at-age supplied via the `weight` data sheet. Forecasts re-use the terminal-year weight schedule. |
| `1` | `"vonBertalanffy"` | von Bertalanffy length-at-age + length-weight allometry (`alpha_wt_len`, `beta_wt_len` on the data control sheet) |
| `2` | `"Richards"` |Sex-specific Richards growth |

### Growth variability, plus group, length bins and maturity

| Argument / column | Values | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `sd_form` | `"SD"` (default), `"CV"` | Whether `sd_L1` / `sd_Linf` are SDs of length-at-age (cm) or CVs (SD = CV x length) -- SS3 `CV_Growth_Pattern` 2 or 0 |
| `sd_plus_group` | `"WHAM"` (default), `"SS3"` | Plus-group SD pinned to the upper endpoint, or interpolated by length. SS3 with `Growth_Age_for_L2 = 999` is `"WHAM"` |
| `plus_group_length` | `"M1"` (default), `"none"`, `"SS3.24"`, `"decay"` | Plus-group mean length: M1-weighted mean toward L-infinity, or SS3's `Linf_decay` -998 / -999 / `plus_group_decay` |
| `pop_lengths` | lower edges (cm); default the data bins | Population length bins on which the age-length key, weight and maturity are integrated |
| `L50_mat_len`, `slope_mat_len` (control sheet) | cm, per cm; default NA | Logistic maturity-at-length; spawning output integrates maturity x weight over length. NA keeps the age-based `maturity` sheet |

Priors and environmental relationships go on growth through `build_growth()`;
see `?build_growth` and `vignette("environmental-linkages-and-priors")`.

Time-varying growth is specified through the linkage grammar rather than a
switch of its own: `build_growth(linkages = list(K = linkage_spec(~ rw(1 | Year))))`
puts a random walk on the von Bertalanffy `K`, and `ar1()` / `(1 | Year)` give
the autoregressive and independent alternatives.

## 9. Harvest control rules (`HCR = build_hcr()`)

| `HCR` | String | Description | Multi-species? |
|:---:|---|---|:---:|
| `0` | `"NoFishing"` | No fishing, estimate hindcast only | Yes |
| `1` | `"CMSY"` | Maximize joint catch across species (option to keep depletion ≥ `Plimit`) | Yes |
| `2` | `"ConstantF"` | Constant F set at `Ftarget` per species | Yes |
| `3` | `"ConstantFSSB"` | F that achieves `Ftarget`% of SB<sub>0</sub> at the end of the projection | Yes |
| `4` | `"ConstantFSPR"` | F<sub>SPR</sub> at `Ftarget` (NEFSC convention; scale via `Fmult`) | No |
| `5` | `"NPFMC"` | NPFMC Tier 3 SPR-based HCR (`Ftarget`, `Flimit`, `Ptarget`, `Plimit`, `Alpha`) | No |
| `6` | `"PFMC"` | PFMC Category 1 `Ptarget`-`Plimit` ACL with uncertainty buffer around `Flimit` (`Pstar`, `Sigma`) | Yes |
| `7` | `"SESSF"` | SESSF Tier 1 SPR-based HCR | No |

`DynamicHCR = TRUE` switches from static to dynamic SB<sub>0</sub>
reference points. `HCRorder` controls the order in which species F is
solved for iterative multi-species HCRs (e.g. predators before prey).
See `?build_hcr`.

## 10. Projection and MSE

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `fit_mod(estimateMode = 2, HCR = build_hcr(...))` | Forward projection under a fixed HCR |
| `sample_rec()` | Bootstrap historical recruitment deviations (with optional `rec_trend`) into the projection; projected recruitment reads them only under `build_srr(proj_mean_rec = FALSE)` |
| `remove_F()` | Refit a model with F = 0 from `styr` (default: the year after `endyr`); `run_mse()` uses it for the no-fishing run behind the collapse metrics |
| `run_mse()` | Closed-loop MSE: refit EM on the `assessment_period` schedule (a period, or the years themselves), sample new data at `sampling_period` |
| `load_mse()` | Reload per-simulation `.rds` files written when `dir =` is supplied |
| `check_mse()` | Validate which OM/EM simulations converged |
| `mse_summary()` | Performance metrics by species, fishery fleet and in total: mean catch, IAV, P(closed), P(F > Flimit), P(SSB < SSBlimit), terminal depletion |

`run_mse()` parallelizes over simulations, on a FORK cluster where the
platform allows one and PSOCK on Windows. The
[MSE vignette](hcrs-and-mses.html) has the seed handling and the
reproducibility guarantees.

## 11. Diagnostics and inference

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `retrospective()` | Peel terminal years and refit; reports Mohn's rho for each quantity / species at the terminal year and the `nyrs_forecast` (default 3) years after it |
| `jitter()` | Refit from random-perturbed starting values; check optimum stability |
| `sim_mod()` / `simulate()` | Simulate data from a fitted model. Observations always; process error (recruitment, M, growth, catchability, selectivity) via `process =`. `simulate()` is the `stats` generic and draws `nsim` replicates at once |
| `self_test()` | Simulate and refit; check the model recovers what generated the data |
| `compare_sim()` | Estimation-vs-truth comparison across simulated replicates |
| `model_average()` | Weighted average of derived quantities across multiple fits, with optional bootstrap uncertainty |
| `reweight_comps()` | Iterative McAllister-Ianelli (1997) tuning of multinomial `Comp_weights` |

## 12. Plotting

Each plotter is named after the quantity it shows: `plot_biomass`, `plot_ssb`,
`plot_recruitment`, `plot_depletion`,
`plot_ssb_depletion`, `plot_exploitable_biomass`, `plot_catch`, `plot_f`,
`plot_mortality`, `plot_m_at_age`, `plot_m2_at_age_prop`, `plot_index`,
`plot_index_residual`, `plot_comp`, `plot_data`, `plot_form`, `plot_b_eaten`,
`plot_b_eaten_prop`, `plot_diet_comp`, `plot_ration`, `plot_selectivity`,
`plot_selectivity_vs_maturity`, `plot_maturity`, `plot_stock_recruit`,
`plot_timeseries`. Most accept a single fitted model or a list of models with
`model_names`.

These are built with **ggplot2** (colorblind-safe Okabe-Ito palette for
discrete series, viridis for continuous ones) and **return the `ggplot`
object**, so they print when called interactively and take further ggplot2
layers (e.g. `plot_biomass(fit) + ggplot2::ggtitle("My title")`). Pass
`file = "stem"` to also write a PNG with a per-plotter suffix
(`plot_recruitment()` writes `stem_R_trajectory.png`); the per-fleet plotters
write one file each, e.g. `stem_comp_annual_fleet<N>_<age|length>.png` from
`plot_comp()`.

**Shared arguments.** The timeseries plotters (`plot_biomass`, `plot_ssb`,
`plot_recruitment`, the depletions, `plot_exploitable_biomass`, `plot_f`), the
predation plotters (`plot_b_eaten`, `plot_b_eaten_prop`, `plot_m_at_age`,
`plot_m2_at_age_prop`, `plot_ration`) and `plot_selectivity` take one common
vocabulary, documented together in `?"rceattle-plot-args"`: `line_col`, `lwd`,
`lty`, `alpha`, `species`, `spnames`, `minyr`, `maxyr`, `incl_proj`,
`incl_mean`, `add_ci`, `model_names`, `file`, `width` and `height`. Each means
the same thing wherever it appears, but not every plotter takes every one
(`incl_mean` is on the predation plotters, `add_ci` only where the quantity
holds standard errors, `alpha` only where the figure has a ribbon or a fan);
check `args()`.

* `line_col` takes colour names, hex codes, or base-graphics palette indices
  (`line_col = 1`), and `lwd` keeps the base-graphics scale where the default
  `3` is a standard-weight line.
* `line_col` and `lty` supply values for whichever variable the *figure*
  separates by colour or line type, which is not always the model (predators in
  `plot_b_eaten_prop()`, sexes in `plot_ration()`); each function's help says
  which. Too few colours are recycled, with a warning. Where colour is a
  magnitude (the year fan in `plot_selectivity()`) `line_col` gives the ramp
  anchors, so `line_col = "black"` draws the fan in black.
* `species` selects (by index, name, logical mask, or `"all"`, in the order
  given) and `spnames` labels.
* `minyr` and `maxyr` narrow the data, not just the axis, so a panel with a free
  y scale rescales to the window.
* Base-graphics arguments (`right_adj`, `top_adj`, `mod_cex`, `legend.pos`,
  `single.plots`, `theta`) are accepted and ignored by the plotters that had
  them, and absent from the rest. Set the equivalent on the returned ggplot
  instead, e.g. `plot_biomass(fit) + ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "right")`.

**Display units.** Numbers-at-age are in thousands of fish and weight-at-age in
kg, so biomass and SSB come out in mt and recruitment in thousands of fish. The
timeseries plotters rescale the axis to `million mt` and `millions`, and derive
the recruitment age from `minage` rather than assuming age 1. Supply inputs on
that convention (catch and index in mt, weight-at-age in kg), or the axis labels
will not describe what is plotted; pass `ylab` to override the derived label.

**Confidence intervals.** `add_ci = TRUE` draws a 95% interval. Strictly
positive series take it on the log scale, `exp(log(x) ± 1.96 · sd_log)`, using
the model's `log_biomass` / `log_ssb` / `log_R` where they exist and the
delta-method identity `sd(log x) = sd(x)/x` where they do not, so it is
right-skewed and cannot reach zero for a weak year class or a depleted stock
(`?plot_timeseries` has the derivation).

`plot_selectivity()` takes it too, but only on a fit run with
`fit_control(selectivity_se = TRUE)` and only for estimated, age-based fleets;
otherwise it warns and draws none. Selectivity is identified only up to a
scalar, so `Sel_norm_bin` fixes the curve's level rather than measuring it: the
pinned bin has a standard error of 0, the band widens away from it, and the
band's shape depends on `Sel_norm_bin` as well as on the information in the
data. Quote that anchor with the interval.

The error comes from whichever `sdreport` the fit ends on. Under
`estimateMode = "Estimate"` with an estimating HCR, `fit_mod()` re-optimizes the
projection with every hindcast parameter fixed, so the standard error of every
selectivity is exactly 0. `estimateMode = "Projection"` estimates no selectivity
at all, and `projection_uncertainty` cannot rescue it. Fit the hindcast alone,
or ask for uncertainty in the projection:

```{r sel-ci, eval = FALSE}
# Errors from the hindcast fit, the usual choice for a selectivity figure.
mod <- fit_mod(data_list = data, estimateMode = "Hindcast",
               fit_control = fit_control(selectivity_se = TRUE))
plot_selectivity(mod, add_ci = TRUE, minyr = 2015, maxyr = 2015)

# Or keep the HCR projection and reuse the hindcast parameters in it.
mod <- fit_mod(data_list = data, HCR = build_hcr(HCR = 5),
               fit_control = fit_control(selectivity_se = TRUE,
                                         projection_uncertainty = TRUE))
```

`fit_mod()` warns when the combination would report zeros, and
`plot_selectivity()` declines to draw a band that is 0 wide at every age. Give
`minyr` / `maxyr` a single year on a time-varying fleet: every year drawn gets
its own band.

Under `random_sel = FALSE` the annual deviations are penalized rather than
integrated, so the band is a penalized-likelihood error conditional on
`Sel_curve_pen1` / `Sel_curve_pen2` and on a fixed `Time_varying_sel_sd`: change
the smoothing and both the curve and its band move. The band is also marginal.
Selectivity error is strongly correlated with F and q, so propagating it into a
derived quantity needs the covariance
(`fit_control(getReportCovariance = TRUE)`), not this interval alone.
